I still feel deeply ashamed of my sagging jawline and worn-out appearance, and I just can't shake the feeling that it's all people see.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever tried to get these appearance concerns checked by a doctor or cosmetic specialist, and if so, what did they tell you? Do you feel the worry is mainly about how you look, or more about being judged because of it?\n\nPatient: I haven't seen any cosmetic specialists or other doctors for this, except for my primary care doctor who referred me to you. When I look in the mirror or under bright lights, the loose skin and wrinkles look so clear and terrible that I know others must see them the exact same way. My family tries to reassure me, but I truly feel they are just being nice to protect my feelings.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever believed that other people are specifically talking about, mocking, or targeting you because of these appearance concerns, or is your worry mainly about how you look and being judged for it?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think people are actively targeting or mocking me. It is just that I feel incredibly self-conscious and ashamed of my aging appearance, and I constantly worry about how worn out I must look to others.\n\nDoctor: When you avoid family events or work presentations, is it mainly because you fear people will judge your appearance, or because you worry you will act awkwardly, blush, or say something embarrassing in front of others?\n\nPatient: It is entirely because of how I look, not because I'm worried about acting awkwardly or saying the wrong thing. I just dread the thought of people seeing my saggy skin and wrinkles in bright light, or being captured in photographs at these events. I feel so ashamed of looking old and worn out that I would rather just avoid being seen at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had similar concerns about other parts of your body or appearance, or is this problem limited to your face and neck?\n\nPatient: No, my concerns are strictly limited to my face and neck, and I don't really worry about any other parts of my body. It is just that I feel incredibly self-conscious and ashamed of my aging appearance, and I constantly worry about how worn out I must look to others.\n\nDoctor: When you avoid family events or work presentations, is it mainly because you fear people will judge your appearance, or because you worry you will act awkwardly, blush, or say something embarrassing in front of others?\n\nPatient: It is entirely because of how I look, not because I'm worried about acting awkwardly or saying the wrong thing. I just dread the thought of people seeing my saggy skin and wrinkles in bright light, or being captured in photographs at these events. I feel so ashamed of looking old and worn out that I would rather just avoid being seen at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had similar concerns about other parts of your body or appearance, or is this problem limited to your face and neck?\n\nPatient: No, my concerns are strictly limited to my face and neck, and I don't really worry about any other parts of my body. Even though my husband and daughter constantly reassure me and tell me I look fine, their words never feel true or reassuring to me. Deep down, I feel certain that I look worn out and saggy, and I am terrified of others seeing me in bright lighting, which is why I try so hard to hide my neck.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel anxious in social situations mainly because you might blush, tremble, or say something embarrassing, even when your appearance is not an issue? I only feel anxious because I dread people seeing my wrinkles and the saggy skin under my jaw, especially in bright light or photos. If I felt my appearance was fine, I wouldn't have any anxiety at all in these situations.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any moment of doubt that these appearance flaws might be less noticeable to others than they seem to you, or are you completely certain they are obvious and severe?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, it just feels so obvious and real to me when I look in the mirror, but I haven't thought about it in terms of how certain I am. I just know that the loose skin and wrinkles are all I can see, and it makes me feel incredibly ashamed to be seen.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe these appearance flaws are definitely real and obvious to everyone, or do you think they might be exaggerated by your mind compared with how others see you?\n\nPatient: My husband and daughter try to reassure me and say it's not that bad, but I am completely convinced that the loose skin and lines are highly visible to everyone. When I look in the mirror, it feels so real and undeniable to me. Even though my husband and daughter try to reassure me otherwise, their words don't help because when I look in the mirror, the loose skin and wrinkles are completely undeniable.\n\nDoctor: When you are with other people, is your main fear that they will notice and judge your appearance, or that you will be embarrassed, awkward, blush, tremble, or say the wrong thing even if your appearance were fine?\n\nPatient: My fear is entirely about people noticing how saggy and worn out my face and neck look, not about blushing, trembling, or saying the wrong thing. If I felt my appearance was fine, I wouldn't have any of this anxiety or feel the need to avoid these situations at all. The distress I feel is completely focused on how I look.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever think there is a chance that your appearance concerns might be more severe in your mind than they appear to other people, or are you completely convinced that the flaws are truly as obvious and severe as they feel to you?"

I just know that the loose skin and wrinkles are all I can see, and it makes me feel incredibly ashamed to be seen.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe these appearance flaws are definitely real and obvious to everyone, or do you think they might be exaggerated by your mind compared with how others see you?\n\nPatient: My husband and daughter try to reassure me and say it's not that bad, but I am completely convinced that the loose skin and lines are highly visible to everyone. When I look in the mirror, it feels so real and undeniable to me.
